summary: The agent implemented a real opt-in retention pass and passed all baseline tests plus 11 of 13 new tests, but it fails to retain synthetic Parent fields and methods referenced through Child, leaving the emitted Java uncompilable.

details.reasoning: The fixed-point retention structure is plausible, but ReferenceAwareSyntheticRetention.findReferencedCandidates constructs an exact field or method key from the token className and only retains an exact candidate match. The failing scenarios emit Child.needed and Child.needed(), while the generated declarations are on Parent. Because inherited declarations are not resolved, neither candidate is retained and javac reports missing symbols.

quick_failure_summary: Inherited generated field and method references through Child are not mapped to their Parent declarations, so the decompiled Java does not compile.

justification.issue_description: Reference resolution does not follow superclass or interface declarations for generated fields and methods. Candidates are keyed by their declaration owner, but references are matched only against the syntactic owner recorded by the emitted token.
justification.evidence: The prompt requires declaring a generated member when the emitted Java refers to it and defines a reference as a use of a member by emitted code. The failing source uses Child.needed and Child.needed(), whose declarations are in Parent. In the agent patch, findReferencedCandidates at ReferenceAwareSyntheticRetention.java:102-112 builds field/method keys directly from token.className and compares them to candidates; the visible codebase also has FieldExprent superclass traversal and StructClass.getMethodRecursive for inherited lookup.
justification.verdict_reasoning: An inherited Java member use is still a reference to the generated declaration, so the missing owner resolution violates the explicit reference-retention behavior and is foreseeable from the Java semantics and repository APIs. This is an agent implementation gap rather than an undocumented test convention or a broken verifier; FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is the appropriate primary verdict.

problem_assessment.notes: The description clearly specifies opt-in behavior, code-only references, omission closure, per-member retention, same-file nested bodies, reconstruction dependence, and determinism. Resolving inherited Java members is a standard consequence of those semantics. The dynamic tests compile deterministic fixtures and the task is challenging but fair.

evidence: junit_base.xml reports 3 baseline tests with 0 failures and 0 errors.
junit_new.xml reports 13 new tests with 11 passing and 2 assertion failures; both failures are javac diagnostics from emitted source, not bootstrap or runtime crashes.

test_execution.log shows the evaluator compiled the solution and ran both test tasks successfully enough to produce JUnit results; the new-task failures are specifically the missing Child.needed field and method symbols.

The trajectory includes a long local Gradle validation detour: a broad './gradlew test --tests org.jetbrains.java.decompiler.OptionParserTest' run ended because the unrelated idea-not-null:test task had no matching tests, but the agent continued and the relevant evaluator run was not blocked.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external environment or verifier blocker explains the failures; the relevant tests executed and directly exposed incomplete inherited-member resolution.
